content: Photophobia refers to discomfort or pain in the eyes when exposed to bright light. It is a relatively common symptom and, in many cases, is not associated with any underlying disease. However, severe photophobia can occur in conjunction with certain eye conditions and may result in significant eye pain, even in dim lighting. Symptoms of Photophobia: Blurred vision Changes in hearing Dizziness Headache Itching Nausea Neck stiffness Numbness or tingling sensations in other parts of the body Eye pain Redness of the eye Presence of a sore or wound in the eye Swelling around the eye Causes of Photophobia: Acute iritis or uveitis, which involve inflammation inside the eye Burns to the eye Corneal abrasions Corneal ulcers Use of certain drugs, including amphetamines, atropine, cocaine, cyclopentolate, idoxuridine, phenylephrine, scopolamine, trifluridine, tropicamide, and vidarabine Prolonged or improper use of contact lenses, or wearing poorly fitted contact lenses Eye diseases, injuries, or infections, such as chalazion, episcleritis, or glaucoma Recent eye testing involving pupil dilation Meningitis Migraine headaches Diagnostic Process: A healthcare provider will conduct a physical examination, including a detailed eye examination. You may be asked specific questions to help determine the cause of your light sensitivity, such as: When did the sensitivity to light begin? Is the discomfort constant or intermittent? How severe is the sensitivity? Do you need to wear dark glasses or stay in dark rooms to alleviate symptoms? Have your pupils been dilated recently during an eye exam? Have you used any eye drops? Do you wear contact lenses? Have you applied any soaps, lotions, cosmetics, or other chemicals near your eyes? Have you been exposed to dust, wind, sunlight, pollen, or chemicals? Does anything improve or worsen the sensitivity? Have you experienced any eye injuries? What medications are you currently taking? Are there any other symptoms accompanying the light sensitivity? The following diagnostic tests may be performed: Corneal scraping Lumbar puncture Pupil dilation Slit-lamp examination When to Seek Urgent Medical Care: If you experience severe eye pain, it is essential to consult a healthcare provider to identify the underlying cause of your light sensitivity. Proper treatment can often resolve the issue. Seek immediate medical attention if: The pain is moderate to severe, even in low-light conditions. You need to wear sunglasses indoors due to the severity of the sensitivity. The sensitivity is accompanied by headaches, red eyes, blurred vision, or does not improve within one to two days.
